definitions.explanation: A person who has received a doctoral degree; an academic title.
A person with extensive knowledge in a particular field; often used colloquially or in nicknames.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{工学|こうがく}{博士|はかせ}の{学位|がくい}を{持|も}っている。
examples.english: He has a PhD in engineering.

examples.japanese: うちの{子|こ}は{恐竜|きょうりゅう}{博士|はかせ}と{呼|よ}ばれている。
examples.english: My child is called a dinosaur expert.
examples.notes: Colloquial use for someone very knowledgeable

examples.japanese: {博士|はかせ}{課程|かてい}を{修了|しゅうりょう}した。

notes:
USAGE: {博士|はかせ} can refer to (1) an academic doctoral degree holder, or (2) colloquially, an expert in something. The reading はくし is also used in formal/academic contexts.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{博士|はかせ}{号|ごう} (doctoral degree)
・{博士|はかせ}{課程|かてい} (doctoral program)
・{博士|はかせ}{論文|ろんぶん} (doctoral thesis)
・〜{博士|はかせ} (Dr. ~, expert in ~)

ACADEMIC DEGREES:
・{学士|がくし} (bachelor's degree)
・{修士|しゅうし} (master's degree)
・{博士|はかせ}/{博士|はくし} (doctorate)

NOTE: In formal academic contexts, {博士|はくし} (on-reading) is preferred. {博士|はかせ} (kun-reading) is more colloquial and used in titles like 「〜博士」.
